title: how do u feel about creating a game with ai code and hand made art?
author: GoDz_Matt_115
selftext: do u think it's possible to do it with no code experience?

comments.author: Savage_PrawnYT
comments.body:
Yes this is definitely possible depending on how you work with Ai. 

This is because with no code experience “you don’t know what you don’t know” there for you need to assume this at every step and ask good questions. Ask the Ai to ask you good questions too. You’ll be fine. Go for it.

replies.author: kilographix
replies.body: I'm building a game right now with nearly 0 coding experience and trying to do pretty much exactly this. The most important part is guardrails, keeping files well organized and enforcing the organizational structure, having test guidelines, code standards/version control/etc in place.

comments.author: abitdaft1776
comments.body:
Yeah man, just do it.

If you want to learn to code, here is what i do.

Scope the game in claude/codex. Make it small game. Like...real fucking small. 

Have the LLM build you a lesson plan in .html with checkboxes you can mark off.  Tell it not to put specific code in the plan, but to instead refer you to the applicable portion of the game engine's documentation.  Then if you can't figure out how to do whatever you need to do, ask it to give you a hint.

replies.author: MiraculousMayhem
replies.body: Man this is simple but GENIUS! Thank you!

replies.author: abitdaft1776
replies.body: Yeah, there is a bit more to my scope.  It keeps track of questions I asks and predicts those types of questions for the next lesson.  It also explains why one way and not another.

replies.author: MiraculousMayhem
replies.body: That's awesome, man. I'm going to have to take a page out of your playbook

comments.author: AlmostLiminal
comments.body: Trivial to make a bad game.  Making a good game means learning everything, including what you don't know that you don't know.

comments.author: Hanfkeks_
comments.body:
Just do it. Coders are rarely Luddites, so if the output is fine, they won't care about how it was achieved.
Artists on the other hand are very conservative and don't handle the changing world very well. They're basically at war with AI.

replies.author: Key_Programmer_5793
replies.body: Designer who loves AI here. Code has always been my bottleneck. These new tools match my curiosity/creativity.

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: llms can make a bad to ok game with no coding, when stuff breaks and the llm doesn't know where to go is where the knowledge is. You can probably do some research to get over those roadblocks and learn a bit along the way.

comments.author: sarahbearahxox
comments.body: Aslong as art and the creative side isn’t ai I’m all for it. Ai code is the same as human code. If it works it works.

comments.author: Anarye
comments.body: Whatever boats your float homie. There isnt a wrong or right way

comments.author: thvaz
comments.body: If you know a bit about coding I guess it is possible, And you will avoid the haters, as no one hates AI being used for anything other than art...

comments.author: count023
comments.body: absolutely nothing wrong with that approach and how i've been working for a while.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
It doesnt matter how we feel. We live in a world where some people still struggle with basic web searches. 

One 'no code' person can succeed while another 'no code' person can fail. Just saying 'no code' doesnt tell us anything

If i have to guess, I would guess that you probably won't do it. Whenever I see a post like this, OP never comes back with  a follow-up. 

Feel free to prove me wrong though

comments.author: Enjoyooooor
comments.body: Full send it. Be prepared for hate all of it is good feedback

comments.author: TimelyBodybuilder121
comments.body: The code part is the one AI does best. Using pure AI gen art is more likely to give you extra work imho.
